planting.note: Root short stem-tip cuttings in barely damp, well-drained mix or a perlite/sphagnum blend; keep humidity high until new roots form, since the thin trailing stems have little moisture reserve.

directions: This small creeping-to-trailing peperomia is distinguished by its slender, wiry stems densely covered in fine hairs and often flushed red to maroon, carrying small, rounded, fleshy green leaves spaced closely along the stem. It forms a low, fine-textured mat or short cascade rather than a climbing habit, making it well suited to terrariums, shallow dish gardens, and small hanging containers where its delicate scale can be appreciated up close. Grow in bright, indirect light with high ambient humidity and allow the mix to dry slightly between waterings, since the thin stems and small leaves offer little buffer against rot in soggy soil. Like many small epiphytic peperomias, it benefits from a coarse, fast-draining substrate rather than standard dense potting mix.
